title: Prefill scorer heuristic compiler and quant tagging
author: Lina Zhou
release_notes: Adds a prefill scoring compiler to generate tenant-aware defaults and attaches per-request quantization tags to telemetry for downstream unit-econ analysis.
description:
Summary: Introduce a prefill scoring compiler that converts workload signals into deterministic default prefill/batching/caching suggestions and emits quantization-tagged telemetry so downstream econ tooling can correlate unit economics with quant profiles. Motivation: Default heuristics are currently noisy across tenants; operations teams request a deterministic, auditable way to derive defaults from sampled traffic, and Research needs request-level quant tagging so regression/delta analysis can surface when quant profiles impact quality-cost tradeoffs. This change bundles three cross-cutting pieces into a single, test-covered PR.

What changed (high level):
- pkg/econ/scorer: new deterministic prefill Scorer with compiled rule pipeline (score, effect estimate, confidence).
- pkg/econ/compiler: compiler that compiles tenant-level workload histograms into static default sets (batch size, cache window, quant profile).
- telemetry/annotator: attaches quant_profile and prefill_score attributes to request telemetry events and spans.
- cmd/prefill-sim: lightweight simulator to validate compiled defaults against sampled traces (used by integration tests).
- docs/operations/prefill-compiler.md: usage and migration notes for Platform/SEs.
- tests/*: unit and integration tests, plus a small e2e using a synthetic tenant trace.

Design notes and compatibility:
- The compiler emits an immutable Defaults object per tenant version; Defaults are intended to be suggested values surfaced to the Console and optionally auto-applied by the policy engine. Defaults carry a confidence score and an opaque compiler-version tag so rollbacks and audits can be performed.
- Telemetry adds two optional string fields: telemetry.prefill_score and telemetry.quant_profile_tag. Both are optional to avoid breaking existing consumers; annotator only populates them when the request traverses a node with the annotator middleware (hosted and Dedicated paths).
- Quant tags are stable strings derived from the quant profile name + short hash to allow cheap grouping in analytics pipelines.

Why this is different from previous prefills:
- Deterministic compiler (not heuristic service) — compiled defaults are stable artifacts that can be versioned and audited.
- Per-request quant tagging — previously quant profiles were only visible at deployment time; now telemetry can tie per-request outcomes to the quant profile used, enabling precise unit-econ regressions and cohorting.
- Lightweight simulator included to validate defaults before any auto-apply action.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy annotator to hosted inference edge (reads optional fields, safe to deploy).
2) Run compiler in dry-run mode for 48h and surface suggested defaults to Console (no auto-apply).
3) Run simulation reports for top 10 tenants and review with SRE/solutions.
4) Flip platform flag to opt-in auto-apply for non-critical tenants behind canary.

If rollback is required:
- Defaults are only suggestions until auto-apply flag is set; disabling the flag prevents further auto-applies. Any applied defaults can be reverted using the Defaults history endpoint (documented).
